title: Cohomology of $\PP^n$, Serre 1954
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X=\PP^n_k$, $\cO(m):=\cO_X(m)$, and
$S^m(V)$ the $m$-th symmetric power of $V=k^{n+1}$.

$$
H^0(X,\cO(m))=S^m(V)\ (m\ge0),\qquad
H^q(X,\cO(m))=0\ (q\notin\{0,n\}),
$$

$$
H^n(X,\cO(m))=0\ (m\ge-n),\qquad
H^n(X,\cO(m))=S^{-m-n-1}(V)^{\vee}\ (m\le-n-1),
$$

the two top-degree clauses for $n\ge1$; for $n=0$, $X=\Spec k$ and
every $\cO(m)$ is $\cO_X$, so $H^0(X,\cO(m))=k$ for all $m$ and there is
no higher cohomology. In particular (for all $n\ge0$)
$\omega_X=\cO_X(-n-1)$ and $H^q(X,\cO_X)=k\cdot\delta_{q,0}$.

Here $n,q\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, and all displayed equalities of modules mean $k$-linear isomorphisms (and the canonical-sheaf equality means an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules). Projective space and its twists are those of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]; $H^q$ is the Zariski module-sheaf cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology]. The ordered basis $x_0,\ldots,x_n$ identifies $S^r(V)$ with the homogeneous degree-$r$ polynomials for $r\ge0$, and $W^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(W,k)$. We use $\omega_X:=\Lambda^n\Omega^1_{X/k}$, with relative differentials as in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and sheaf exterior powers as in [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power].

proof.text: First take $n=0$. The $n=0$ clause of [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology], with $A=k$, identifies $X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k$, every twist with a free rank-one module, and all its positive cohomology with zero. Its global sections are therefore $k$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$. Also $\omega_X=\Lambda^0\Omega^1_{X/k}=\mathcal O_X$ by [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], and $\mathcal O_X(-1)\cong\mathcal O_X$ by the same rank-one assertion. Thus the canonical-sheaf clause holds in dimension zero as well. In the remaining steps assume $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 01XT, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof (ordered Cech complex and exponent-vector decomposition)

proof.text: Use the standard cover $U_i=D_+(x_i)$, ordered by $0<\cdots<n$. It covers $X$ because a homogeneous prime defining a point of $\operatorname{Proj}k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ cannot contain every $x_i$. Every nonempty intersection $U_J=D_+(\prod_{j\in J}x_j)$ is affine by [def-pc-proj]. The twist is locally free of rank one by [def-pc-projective-space-twist], hence quasi-coherent: on each chart it is the sheaf associated to the free rank-one chart module. Thus [lem-pc-cech-computes] identifies its Cech cohomology with $H^q(X,\mathcal O(m))$. Apply [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes] to replace the full complex by its ordered complex. Finally [lem-pc-twist-cech-monomial-decomposition], with $A=k,d=m$, identifies that complex with $\bigoplus_{\sum e_i=m}C_e^\bullet$, preserving the monomial labels and the differential.

source.place: Tag 01XT, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof (ordered Cech complex and exponent-vector decomposition)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-monomial-cech-complex-homology] to each exponent vector. An exponent vector with no negative entries contributes one copy of $k$ in degree zero; a vector with all entries negative contributes one copy in degree $n$; a vector with some but not all entries negative contributes nothing. Taking cohomology commutes here with the direct sum: the differential preserves each summand, so a finite-support element is a cycle exactly when each component is a cycle, and it is a boundary exactly when each component is a boundary (choose preimages for its finitely many nonzero components). Consequently $H^0$ has basis $x^e$ for $e_i\ge0,\sum e_i=m$, $H^n$ has basis $[x^e]$ for $e_i<0,\sum e_i=m$, and $H^q=0$ for $q\notin\{0,n\}$. These identifications are $k$-linear and the bases are $k$-bases: with $A=k$, [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] states the same monomial descriptions as isomorphisms of $A$-modules, the degree-$n$ class of $x^e$ being that of the Cech $n$-cochain $x^e$ on $U_0\cap\cdots\cap U_n$.

source.place: Tag 01XT, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof (ordered Cech complex and exponent-vector decomposition)

proof.text: For $m\ge0$, the degree-zero basis from the preceding step is precisely the monomial basis of $k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_m=S^m(V)$, with $V$ the free space on the ordered coordinates. The identification of this graded piece with the symmetric power is explicitly included in clause (i) of [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology], applied to $A=k,d=m$. This gives the claimed $H^0$ identification. For the top-degree vanishing, every surviving exponent has $e_i\le-1$, so $m=\sum e_i\le-n-1$. Hence there are no such vectors if $m\ge-n$, proving the asserted $H^n$ vanishing.

source.place: Tag 01XT, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof (ordered Cech complex and exponent-vector decomposition)

proof.text: If $m\le-n-1$, set $r=-m-n-1\ge0$. The assignment $e\mapsto f=-e-\mathbf1$ is a bijection from strictly negative vectors of sum $m$ to nonnegative vectors of sum $r$, with inverse $f\mapsto-f-\mathbf1$. The latter set is finite, since $0\le f_i\le r$. Send the basis vector $[x^e]$ of $H^n$ to the coordinate functional on $S^r(V)$ which is $1$ on the monomial $x^{-e-\mathbf1}$ and $0$ on all other monomials. These are precisely the dual basis of this finite monomial basis, so the resulting linear map is an isomorphism $H^n(X,\mathcal O(m))\cong S^{-m-n-1}(V)^\vee$.

source.place: Tag 01XT, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof (ordered Cech complex and exponent-vector decomposition)

proof.text: For the canonical-sheaf assertion with $n\ge1$, apply [lem-pc-projective-space-canonical] with $A=k$. Its sheaf $\omega_P$ is exactly $\Lambda^n\Omega^1_{X/k}$, and its stated isomorphism sends the local generator $\eta_i=(-1)^i\bigwedge_{j\ne i}d(x_j/x_i)$ to the local generator of $\mathcal O(-n-1)$. Thus it supplies the asserted canonical-bundle isomorphism, independently of the calculation of vector-space dimensions. The dimension-zero case was treated in step 1.

source.place: node lem-pc-projective-space-canonical, statement and local-generator formula

proof.text: Take $m=0$. In dimension $n\ge1$, the only nonnegative exponent vector of sum zero is $(0,\ldots,0)$, so $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k\cdot1$. No strictly negative vector has sum zero, so the top group vanishes, and all other positive groups already vanish by step 3. Step 1 gives the same assertion when $n=0$. This proves $H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)=k\cdot\delta_{q,0}$ for every $n\ge0$.
